package.name: glibc-neutered-2.44
package.description: the GNU C library (Werewolf fixed hardening policy)

pipeline.name: Fetch the locked source commit
pipeline.runs:
git init -q .
for delay in 0 15 45; do
  sleep "$delay"
  for source in https://github.com/kraj/glibc.git https://sourceware.org/git/glibc.git; do
    if git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c fetch.fsckObjects=true fetch --no-tags --depth=1 "$source" 34106fee698c83eb0af71d4d0381e66b399be746; then
      test "$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)" = 34106fee698c83eb0af71d4d0381e66b399be746
      git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout -q --detach 34106fee698c83eb0af71d4d0381e66b399be746
      exit 0
    fi
  done
done
echo "34106fee698c83eb0af71d4d0381e66b399be746: every source failed, three times" >&2
exit 1

pipeline.name: Apply Werewolf policy patches
pipeline.runs:
while IFS= read -r name; do
  patch -p1 --forward --batch --fuzz=2 --no-backup-if-mismatch -i "patches/$name" || exit 1
done < patches/series

pipeline.name: Set up build directory
pipeline.runs: mkdir build

pipeline.name: Configure glibc
pipeline.runs:
cd build
echo "user-defined-trusted-dirs=/usr/local/lib:/usr/local/lib64:/usr/lib:/usr/lib64:/lib:/lib64" >> configparms.base
echo "slibdir=/usr/lib" >> configparms.base
echo "libdir=/usr/lib" >> configparms.base
echo "rootsbindir=/usr/bin" >> configparms.base
echo "build-programs=no" > configparms
# If x86_64, set to /lib64, /lib for aarch64
if [ ${{build.arch}} == "x86_64" ]; then
  echo "rtlddir=/lib64" >> configparms.base
else
  echo "rtlddir=/lib" >> configparms.base
fi
cat configparms.base >> configparms

../configure \
  --prefix=/usr \
  --libdir=/usr/lib \
  --datadir=/usr/share \
  --includedir=/usr/include \
  --sbindir=/usr/bin \
  --host=${{host.triplet.gnu}} \
  --build=${{host.triplet.gnu}} \
  --enable-bind-now \
  --enable-fortify-source \
  --enable-stackguard-randomization \
  --enable-stack-protector=strong \
  --enable-cet \
  --with-pkgversion="glibc-${{package.full-version}}" \
  --disable-build-nscd \
        --disable-nscd \
        --enable-hardcoded-path-in-tests \
        --disable-werror \
  --disable-crypt \
  --enable-kernel=6.18

echo 'override rtld-prefix =' >> configparms.base
echo 'override rtld-prefix =' >> configparms
echo 'include $(common-objpfx)../tests/harness.mk' >> configparms.base
echo 'include $(common-objpfx)../tests/harness.mk' >> configparms
echo 'CFLAGS += -fstrict-flex-arrays=3' >> configparms.base
echo 'CFLAGS += -fstrict-flex-arrays=3' >> configparms
echo 'LDFLAGS.so += -Wl,-z,separate-code' >> configparms.base
echo 'LDFLAGS.so += -Wl,-z,separate-code' >> configparms
echo 'LDFLAGS-rtld += -Wl,-z,separate-code' >> configparms.base
echo 'LDFLAGS-rtld += -Wl,-z,separate-code' >> configparms
make -C build -j$(nproc)

# Build the programs with fortify
echo "build-programs=yes" > build/configparms
cat build/configparms.base >> build/configparms
make -C build -j$(nproc)
make -C build -j$(nproc) install DESTDIR="${{targets.destdir}}"

pipeline.name: Configure built-in NSS providers for validation
pipeline.runs: cp profile/nsswitch.conf /etc/nsswitch.conf

pipeline.name: Install explicit locale test fixtures
pipeline.runs: werewolf-tools/package-helper --action locales

pipeline.name: Verify fixed hardening policy
pipeline.runs: werewolf-tools/package-helper --action policy

pipeline.name: Run the glibc testsuite
pipeline.runs:
if [ -d /usr/lib/oldglibc ]; then
  echo "oldglibc detected: skipping the glibc testsuite (glibc-2.44 is dev-headers-only in this environment)"
  exit 0
fi

# The glibc test suite runs in two phases (upstream Makerules
# check-twopass), which we gate differently:
#
#   Phase 1 (run-built-tests=no): builds every test program and runs the
#   "special" tests -- header/conformance/ABI checks that do not execute a
#   compiled binary (conform/*, check-installed-headers, check-abi-*, ...).
#   This phase is REQUIRED to pass. Known pre-existing special-test failures
#   are allow-listed in allowed-failures.txt (consumed by upstream's
#   summarize-tests); any new special-test failure fails the build.
#
#   Phase 2 (run-built-tests=yes): runs the compiled test binaries. Many of
#   these are timing-sensitive or depend on privileges/features unavailable
#   in the sandboxed build (e.g. setuid, aarch64 BTI), so they are flaky or
#   expected to fail here. We do NOT hard-gate this phase; instead the
#   glibc-testresults subpackage enforces a pass/fail ratio over the full
#   result set.
#
# We invoke the phases explicitly (instead of `make check`) so phase 2's
# failures do not fail the build while phase 1 stays required.
make -C build -j$(nproc) run-built-tests=no tests
make -C build -j$(nproc) run-built-tests=yes tests || true

pipeline.name: Set up ldconfig
pipeline.runs:
mkdir -p "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc
cp vendor/ld.so.conf "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc

cp vendor/ld.so.conf.d/*.conf "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/ld.so.conf.d

pipeline.runs:

pipeline.name: Generate public ABI report
pipeline.runs:
# Snapshot the public ABI of the core glibc libraries with abi-dumper.
# This must run before the strip step, while the libraries still carry
# DWARF debug info. -public-headers restricts the detailed symbol info
# to interfaces declared in glibc's installed public headers, filtering
# out private/internal symbols.
report_dir="${{targets.destdir}}/usr/share/abi-reports/${{package.name}}-${{package.version}}"
mkdir -p "$report_dir"
for so in "${{targets.destdir}}"/usr/lib/lib*.so.*; do
  # Only dump real shared objects, not the symlinks pointing at them.
  [ -L "$so" ] && continue
  lib=$(basename "$so")
  # These are built with incompatible options and can't be dumped.
  # We should try to investigate at point, but dumping libc is
  # more important so just ignore these for now.
  [ "$lib" = "libnss_dns.so.2" ] && continue
  [ "$lib" = "libnss_files.so.2" ] && continue
  abi-dumper "$so" \
    -o "$report_dir/${lib%.so.*}.dump" \
    -lver "${{package.version}}" \
    -public-headers "${{targets.destdir}}/usr/include"
done

pipeline.name: Check libc public ABI against the previous report
pipeline.runs:
# Compare the freshly generated libc ABI dump against the previously
# published one (installed via the glibc-abi-report build dependency) so
# we can catch ABI regressions at build time.
old_dump="$(find /usr/share/abi-reports/ -name libc.dump -print -quit)"
new_dump="${{targets.destdir}}/usr/share/abi-reports/${{package.name}}-${{package.version}}/libc.dump"
if [ ! -f "$old_dump" ]; then
  echo "No baseline ABI report at $old_dump! Nothing to compare to."
  exit 1
else
  report_path="${{targets.destdir}}/usr/share/abi-reports/${{package.name}}-${{package.version}}/update-report.html"
  # abi-compliance-checker exits non-zero on any incompatibility. Don't
  # block the build on that here, we grade compatibility ourselves below.
  abi-compliance-checker -l libc -old "$old_dump" -new "$new_dump" \
    -report-path "$report_path" || true
  # make sure we actually generate the report, since we're masking the exit code from generating it.
  test -f "$report_path"
  # Fail the build if binary ABI compatibility drops below the threshold.
  ./compatibility-gate --kind binary --threshold 98.0 "$report_path"
fi

  exit 0
fi
cd build/
# Move all the test results and log files
find . \( -name "*.test-result" -o -name "*.out" \) \
  -exec sh -c 'dir=$(dirname $1); mkdir -p $2/$dir; cp $1 $2/$dir' _ {} $resultdir \;
cp tests.sum $resultdir

pipeline.name: Adapt apk test tooling to strict option ordering
pipeline.runs:
mv /usr/bin/apk /usr/bin/apk.real
for app in info add del version update; do ln -s apk.real "/usr/bin/apk_$app"; done
cat > /usr/bin/apk <<'NEUTERED_APK'
#!/bin/sh
case "$1" in
  info|add|del|version|update) app=$1; shift; exec "/usr/bin/apk_$app" "$@" ;;
  *) exec /usr/bin/apk.real "$@" ;;
esac
NEUTERED_APK
chmod 755 /usr/bin/apk
test "$(apk version -t 0-r0 1-r0)" = '<'
if test -n '${{vars.neutered-test-repository}}'; then
  printf '%s\n' '${{vars.neutered-test-repository}}' 'https://packages.wolfi.dev/os' > /etc/apk/repositories
  apk update
fi

pipeline.name: Verify PASS/FAIL ratio in test result files is within acceptable threshold
pipeline.runs:
set -euo pipefail
if [ -d /usr/lib/oldglibc ]; then
  echo "glibc testsuite was skipped in this environment (oldglibc detected); nothing to verify"
  exit 0
fi
MAX_FAIL_RATIO=0.055
fail_count=$(find /usr/share/glibc-testresults -type f -name "*.test-result" -exec /usr/bin/grep "^FAIL:" '{}' ';' 2> /dev/null | wc -l)
pass_count=$(find /usr/share/glibc-testresults -type f -name "*.test-result" -exec /usr/bin/grep "^PASS:" '{}' ';' 2> /dev/null | wc -l)
total=$((pass_count + fail_count))
echo "PASS: $pass_count, FAIL: $fail_count, TOTAL: $total"
[ "$total" -gt 0 ]
fail_ratio=$(awk "BEGIN { printf \"%.4f\", $fail_count / $total }")
echo "Fail ratio: $fail_ratio (max allowed: $MAX_FAIL_RATIO)"
awk "BEGIN { exit ($fail_ratio > $MAX_FAIL_RATIO) ? 1 : 0 }"

pipeline.name: Pin link-time shared objects to this glibc version
pipeline.runs:
ver="${{package.version}}"
dst="${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/lib"
src="${{targets.destdir}}/usr/lib"

# 1. Replace the .so symlinks with real copies of this build's libraries.
#    We want builds against these to target the version of glibc associated with this
#    package, not whatever the current glibc runtime is.
#    glibc runtime owns libfoo.so.1, glibc-dev owns libfoo.so -> libfoo.so.1 symlink
#    we are replacing.
for so in libanl.so libBrokenLocale.so libc_malloc_debug.so \
          libmvec.so libnss_compat.so libnss_db.so \
          libnss_hesiod.so libresolv.so libthread_db.so; do
  [ -L "$dst/$so" ] || continue
  target="$(readlink "$dst/$so")" # e.g. libresolv.so.2
  rm "$dst/$so"
  cp "$src/$target" "$dst/$so"
done

# 2. Pin the libc/libm linker scripts to this version stream.
#    Copy runtime-owned shared objects mentioned by linker scripts into a
#    version-streamed location, modify linker scripts to reference version-streamed
#    copies.
cp "$src/libc.so.6" "$dst/libc.so-$ver"
cp "$src/libm.so.6" "$dst/libm.so-$ver"

pipeline.name: Pin libc.so GROUP to this build's libc.so.6
Pin libm.so GROUP to this build's libm.so.6
Point libm.so AS_NEEDED at our pinned libmvec copy

pipeline.name: libc.so/libm.so are pinned to this version, interp left on runtime
No pinned library references a GLIBC newer than this version
pipeline.runs:
ver="${{package.version}}"; fail=0
for f in /usr/lib/libc.so-$ver /usr/lib/libm.so-$ver \
         /usr/lib/libresolv.so /usr/lib/libanl.so; do
  hi="$(readelf -V "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' \
        | sed 's/GLIBC_//' | sort -V | tail -1)"
  [ -z "$hi" ] && continue
  if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$hi" "$ver" | sort -V | tail -1)" != "$ver" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: $f references GLIBC_$hi > GLIBC_$ver"; fail=1
  fi
done
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS: nothing exceeds GLIBC_$ver"; exit $fail

pipeline.name: Confirm that we're still compatible with current gcc
pipeline.runs:
set -euo pipefail
# This was a problem due to some legacy fix-includes in gcc that interfered
# with new glibc private symbols.  Let's make sure that doesn't break again
cat <<EOF >gcc_test.cc
#include <thread>
#include <future>
int main(void)
{
  return 0;
}
EOF
g++ -o test_build gcc_test.cc
# Test that glibc startup files do not leak into the binary
if [ -n "$(readelf --notes test_build | grep -F '"name":"glibc"')" ]; then
  readelf --notes test_build
  echo glibc package note detected in a shared linked binary
  exit 1
fi

pipeline.name: Verify that frame unwinding doesn't crash (when glibc is compiled with hardening)
A built binary's GLIBC floor is <= this dev version, and it runs without requiring the dev package at runtime
pipeline.runs:
ver="${{package.version}}"
cat > t.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
static void bye(void){}
int main(void){ atexit(bye); printf("%f\n", sqrt(2.0)); return 0; }
EOF
# -fstack-protector-all forces __stack_chk_fail_local, proving the
# libc.so GROUP still pulls in libc_nonshared.a.
gcc -fstack-protector-all t.c -o t -lm
apk del ${{package.name}}-dev gcc
./t
hi="$(readelf -V ./t 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' \
      | sed 's/GLIBC_//' | sort -V | tail -1)"
echo "binary floor: ${hi:-none}, dev version: $ver"
if [ -n "$hi" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$hi" "$ver" | sort -V | tail -1)" != "$ver" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: binary requires GLIBC_$hi > $ver"; exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: floor <= $ver and binary runs"

pipeline.name: Verify apk bootstrap works
pipeline.runs:
set -euo pipefail
check_bootstrap_log() {
  local log="$1"
  cat "$log"
  # Filter out known-ok "updating directory permissions" errors,
  # then fail if any real ERROR: lines remain.
  if grep -e "ERROR:" "$log" | grep -v "updating directory permissions" > errors.log; then
    echo "Unexpected errors found in bootstrap log:"
    cat errors.log
    exit 1
  fi
}

# Verify that glibc + bash-binsh bootstrap works
mkdir -p /tmp/glibc-bash/etc/apk
cp -r /etc/apk/repositories /etc/apk/keys /tmp/glibc-bash/etc/apk
apk add --initdb --root /tmp/glibc-bash glibc bash-binsh &> bootstrap.log || :
check_bootstrap_log bootstrap.log

# Verify that glibc + busybox bootstrap works
mkdir -p /tmp/glibc-busybox/etc/apk
cp -r /etc/apk/repositories /etc/apk/keys /tmp/glibc-busybox/etc/apk
apk add --initdb --root /tmp/glibc-busybox glibc busybox &> bootstrap.log || :
check_bootstrap_log bootstrap.log

pipeline.name: Verify version-streamed virtuals do not resolve to an older package
pipeline.runs:
# Now that glibc is version-streamed, every package it produces is named
# with a version-stream suffix/prefix (e.g. ld-linux-2.43) and provides the
# bare, un-versioned name as a virtual (e.g. ld-linux). Older, non-
# version-streamed packages of those same bare names still exist in the
# index and will remain until they are garbage collected. If one of them
# is still solveable alongside the current glibc, `apk add`-ing the bare
# virtual name could quietly resolve to that stale package instead of the
# one we just built (see the ld-linux case in the commit that added this
# test).
#
# For each virtual, install it in a fresh root alongside glibc
# and confirm the resolved package is not older than what
# we just built. We compare with >= rather than == so that rebuilding
# this version still passes after a newer glibc has been published.
expected="${{package.full-version}}"

virtuals="
  glibc
  glibc-abi-report
  glibc-dev
  glibc-iconv
  glibc-locale-ca
  glibc-locale-de
  glibc-locale-en
  glibc-locale-es
  glibc-locale-extra
  glibc-locale-fr
  glibc-locale-posix
  glibc-locales
  glibc-testresults
  ld-linux
  libc-bin
  libcrypt1
  localedef
  posix-libc-utils
  posix-libc-utils-bin
  sln
  tzutils
"

# Print the version of the installed package that satisfies $1 (matching
# either the package name or one of its provides) in the root at $2.
installed_version() {
  awk -v want="$1" '
    BEGIN { RS = "" }
    {
      pkg = ""; ver = ""; prov = ""
      n = split($0, lines, "\n")
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        if (lines[i] ~ /^P:/)      pkg  = substr(lines[i], 3)
        else if (lines[i] ~ /^V:/) ver  = substr(lines[i], 3)
        else if (lines[i] ~ /^p:/) prov = substr(lines[i], 3)
      }
      matched = (pkg == want)
      if (!matched) {
        m = split(prov, provs, " ")
        for (j = 1; j <= m; j++) {
          name = provs[j]; sub(/=.*/, "", name)
          if (name == want) { matched = 1; break }
        }
      }
      if (matched) { print ver; exit }
    }
  ' "$2/lib/apk/db/installed"
}

rc=0
for v in $virtuals; do
  root="$(mktemp -d)"
  mkdir -p "$root/etc/apk"
  cp -r /etc/apk/repositories /etc/apk/keys "$root/etc/apk/"
  if ! apk add --initdb --root "$root" glibc "$v" > "$root/add.log" 2>&1; then
    echo "FAIL: apk add glibc-${{package.version}} $v failed to solve"
    cat "$root/add.log"
    rc=1
    rm -rf "$root"
    continue
  fi
  got="$(installed_version "$v" "$root")"
  if [ -z "$got" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: apk add glibc-${{package.version}} $v installed nothing satisfying $v"
    rc=1
    rm -rf "$root"
    continue
  fi
  rel="$(apk version -t "$got" "$expected" || true)"
  if [ "$rel" = "<" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: apk add glibc-${{package.version}} $v resolved $v to $got, expected >= $expected"
    rc=1
  else
    echo "PASS: $v resolved to $got (>= $expected)"
  fi
  rm -rf "$root"
done
exit $rc
